question: What claim about the uniqueness of this knowledge must hold if nothing equal to it is said ever to exist again?
premises: Knowledge equal to this knowledge is considered.
Such knowledge will not exist again.
Nor will it exist in the future at all.
inference: The knowledge in question is unique, with nothing equal to it now or in the future.
uncertainties: The referent of anena is not recoverable from this verse alone.
plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this; there will be none again.
